claims.text: The proposed test material is an as-cast, multiphase eutectic high-entropy alloy in an AlCoCrFeNi-based system.
The constituent phases exhibit inherent electrochemical inhomogeneity.
Mo-depleted FCC and Mo-enriched sigma phases have different electrochemical potentials.
Potential differences between FCC and sigma phases create localized galvanic cells.
The localized galvanic cells accelerate oxidation, electron transfer at phase boundaries, and selective dissolution.
Mechanical wear continuously removes or ruptures the surface film and exposes fresh material.
Wear-induced exposure of phases having different potentials intensifies localized galvanic corrosion.
Localized corrosion weakens the alloy and thereby accelerates mechanical wear.
Localized galvanic corrosion is the primary cause of accelerated coupled wear-corrosion degradation at 300 degrees Celsius in a NaCl environment.
An externally applied potential bias can neutralize or minimize electrochemical potential differences between the phases.
Minimizing the interphase electrochemical gradient will suppress localized galvanic-cell formation.
Relative to open circuit, potential bias will significantly reduce localized corrosion current density or localized corrosion rate.
Relative to open circuit, potential bias will reduce corrosion-induced secondary wear acceleration and wear volume.
Relative to open circuit, potential bias will lower the total degradation rate.
Open-circuit exposure permits inherent phase-potential differences to produce synergistic wear-corrosion degradation.
The comparison holds temperature, NaCl exposure, wear load, and duration constant while changing only the electrochemical control condition.
Reliably maintaining an external electrochemical bias at elevated temperature presents technical challenges.

contradictions.description: The proposed material is described as AlCoCrFeNi-based while its example phase contrast requires Mo-depleted FCC and Mo-enriched sigma phases. The cited evidence instead concerns a laser-clad CoCrFeNiMo coating, so the named target composition and the invoked Mo partitioning are not internally aligned unless a Mo-containing AlCoCrFeNi derivative is intended.

The exposure is described as a NaCl-containing atmosphere at 300 degrees Celsius, whereas applied electrochemical bias and Tafel corrosion-current measurements ordinarily require a defined conductive electrolyte and cell configuration. The hypothesis does not specify whether this is a pressurized aqueous electrolyte, molten salt, thin-film electrolyte, or another arrangement.
